newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-INJURY-HIT BAYERN FACE TEST IN COLOGNE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INJURY-HIT BAYERN FACE TEST IN COLOGNE.

text.p: Bayern Munich, beset by injuries and by rumours that international defender Christian Ziege is considering leaving the club, travel to Cologne on Saturday in search of a much-needed win.

The Munich side slipped to third in the Bundesliga last week. Not even victory against sixth-placed Cologne would put them back on top of the table but defeat would leave them trailing badly behind Stuttgart, who meet Rostock and are currently four points ahead.
Bayern will be missing five key players including wing-back Ziege, who has a knee injury, defender Thomas Helmer and defensive midfielder Thomas Strunz.
Cologne will be keen to do well after last week's embarrassing 0-3 defeat to Duisburg, promoted this season from the second division, and will face Bayern untroubled by injuries.

Bayern's president Franz Beckenbauer dismissed rumours that the 24-year-old Ziege was considering transferring abroad after reports that English teams Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur were interested in poaching him.
Tottenham, Juergen Klinsmann's former club, were reported to have offered 12 million marks for Ziege, whose contract with Bayern runs out in 1998.
"That is just not an issue. Christian has an existing contract with us and he is going to keep to it. He is staying with us," Beckenbauer said on Thursday.
But more rumours surfaced in the German press on Friday, saying that Italian teams Juventus and AC Milan had their eye on Ziege and that the former had made him a lucrative offer.
Bayern's star striker Klinsmann, having weathered a bad patch, will take to the pitch with more confidence after he scored for Germany against Armenia in a World Cup qualifier on Wednesday.
It was his first goal since an embarrassing missed penalty against Valencia in the UEFA Cup.
German mass-circulation newspaper Bild asked Klinsmann why he always managed to scored goals for Germany but not -- at least recently -- for Bayern.
"Does he need (Germany trainer) Berti Vogts to score?" was the headline over a story that recounted recent successes with the German team in Yerevan and in a friendly against Poland.
